pl-l4d9c1-d1e115.summary: States that as there are two realities of the sacrament, there are two ways of eating: sacramental, by which good and bad eat, and spiritual, by which only the good eat.
claims: Sacramental eating is common to good and bad; spiritual eating belongs only to the good.

pl-l4d9c1-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: to eat Christ is not only to receive his body in the sacrament, since many receive unworthily, but to remain in him and have him remaining in oneself. One eats spiritually who remains in the unity of Christ and the Church that the sacrament signifies; one who disagrees with Christ neither eats his flesh nor drinks his blood, though he receives the sacrament daily to his judgment.
claims: Spiritual eating is remaining in Christ and the Church.

pl-l4d9c1-d1e133.summary: Quotes Augustine distinguishing spiritual from sacramental eating: why prepare teeth and stomach? Believe, and you have eaten. To believe in him is to eat the bread and wine; whoever believes in him eats him.
claims: To believe in Christ is to eat him spiritually.

pl-l4d9c1-d1e146.summary: Adds Augustine: Christ is to be eaten as he says, 'whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me and I in him'; whoever does not remain in him, though he receives the sacrament, gains great torment.

pl-l4d9c1-d1e152.summary: Adds Augustine: no one should doubt that one shares in the Lord's body and blood when he becomes a member of Christ, and is not cut off from that bread and cup even if he dies in the unity of Christ's body before eating it, since he is not deprived of the sacrament's benefit when found in what it signifies. In the sacrament he commended his body and blood, which he made us; we too have become his body.
claims: A member of Christ shares in his body even without receiving the sacrament.
The faithful have become Christ's body.

pl-l4d9c1-d1e158.summary: Repeats Augustine: one who disagrees with Christ does not eat his flesh or blood, though he receives the sacrament daily to his judgment.
claims: Those at odds with Christ do not eat him spiritually.

pl-l4d9c1.summary: As the sacrament has two realities, there are two ways of eating: sacramental, by good and bad, and spiritual, by the good only. Augustine: to eat Christ is not only to receive his body in the sacrament, which many do unworthily, but to remain in him and have him remaining in oneself; one who disagrees with Christ does not eat his flesh though he receives the sacrament daily to his judgment. 'Believe, and you have eaten.' Whoever becomes a member of Christ shares his body and blood even if he dies before receiving the sacrament.
claims: There are two ways of eating: sacramental and spiritual.
Good and bad eat sacramentally; only the good eat spiritually.
To eat Christ spiritually is to remain in him by faith and unity.
A member of Christ shares in his body even without receiving the sacrament.
